climate.overview_html: The headline new data point on September 8 is the Copernicus C3S August 2026 climate bulletin — confirming August 2026 as the warmest August ever recorded, at 1.65°C above pre-industrial levels, beating August 2024 by 0.14°C, and completing the hottest boreal summer (June–August) on record globally. With eight months of data in hand and the Super El Niño accelerating toward its peak, 2026 now carries roughly 75% probability of becoming the warmest calendar year in the ERA5 record. Daily global sea surface temperature peaked at 21.1°C on August 22 — a new record for any August day, directly fuelling the active hazard roster. The UNEP Limiting Overshoot report (September 2) continues to set the framing context: 1.5°C is now inevitable, overshoot likely peaks at 1.6–1.8°C; the Nepal–Tibet GLOF holds at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing; and EFFIS confirms Europe’s burnt area has reached 649,474 hectares as of the September 7 data refresh — up from 647,579 ha yesterday.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Climate Bulletin: Warmest August on Record at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial — Beats August 2024 by 0.14°C; Completes Hottest Boreal Summer on Record; 2026 Now ~75% Likely to Be Warmest Year in ERA5; SST Hits 21.1°C on August 22 (New August Day Record)
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service August 2026 climate bulletin, published in the first week of September, confirms August 2026 as the warmest August in the ERA5 dataset, reaching 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline — beating the previous August record set in August 2024 (1.51°C) by a wide 0.14°C margin. August 2026 completes the hottest boreal summer (June–August) on record globally. Climatologist Zeke Hausfather notes that with eight months now in the record, 2026 carries approximately 75% probability of becoming the warmest calendar year in ERA5 — the first time a year-end record has been this foreseeable with so many months remaining. Daily global sea surface temperature on August 22 reached 21.1°C, surpassing the prior record of 21.09°C and setting the highest SST reading ever measured for any August day. The developing Super El Niño adds further thermodynamic fuel to what has already been an ocean warming trajectory over multiple decades of human-driven climate change.

items.headline: UNEP Limiting Overshoot Report: 1.5°C Crossing Now Inevitable; Overshoot Likely to Peak at 1.6–1.8°C; Gigatonne-Scale Carbon Dioxide Removal Required to Descend; Every Tenth of a Degree of Peak Warming Still Matters
items.summary: UNEP's September 2 report formally declares that holding global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels is no longer achievable — the world will cross that threshold and is likely to reach a peak of 1.6–1.8°C before large-scale carbon dioxide removal can bring it back down. The report defines 'overshoot' as the period during which global temperature exceeds 1.5°C, and quantifies the consequences: each additional tenth of a degree significantly increases the probability of crossing irreversible tipping points in the Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, the Amazon rainforest, and Atlantic ocean circulation. UNEP argues that even though 1.5°C is now technically overshot, deep immediate emissions cuts still minimise the height of the overshoot, limit the duration above 1.5°C, and reduce reliance on speculative gigaton-scale CDR to return below threshold. The report arrives as the Super El Niño of 2026 is already driving temperatures to anomalous new highs.

items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Near-100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February 2027; 2027 on Track for Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades.' WMO assigned nearly 100% probability that El Niño will persist through at least February 2027. Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 record on the multi-variate ENSO index. Because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, peak atmospheric warming will arrive in 2027, raising the prospect of 2027 becoming the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: STABLE — 1,318+ Dead (1,287 Nepal + 31 Tibet); 5,614+ Missing; Debris 240 km Inside India; Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; 5,000+ Rescuers Active
items.summary: No material change in casualty figures as of September 8: 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet — a combined minimum of 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing. The disaster originated on August 27 from the collapse of a section of Langtang Lirung glacier at approximately 5,200 metres, generating a seismic signal of magnitude Ms 5.2. Debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn surrounding glaciers may still collapse. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations. The event represents one of the deadliest glacial lake outburst floods on instrumental record globally.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 649,474 Hectares Burned (EFFIS Updated September 7) — Very Extreme Fire Danger Persisting Across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, Ukraine; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area of 649,474 hectares as of the September 7 data update — up from 647,579 ha as of September 4. Very extreme fire danger continues across a broad arc from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The 2026 season continues tracking ahead of the long-term 20-year average of 328,010 ha for the same date period, with four of the EU's 15 largest fires of the past decade occurring this summer. Belgium saw its worst wildfire in more than a century in August. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Downgraded to Category 2 (110 mph); Track Shifted to Pass Just West of Niihau & Kauaʻi Overnight Monday–Tuesday; Hurricane Warning in Effect for Kauaʻi County & Niihau; State of Emergency Declared; 129 National Guard Activated; 8–12” Rain; Life-Threatening Surf; Power Outages Likely
major_events.status: CATEGORY 2 · 110 MPH · HW KAUAI COUNTY & NIIHAU · TRACK JUST WEST · OVERNIGHT PASS · STATE OF EMERGENCY
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell has weakened further from Category 3 (115 mph, Sunday) to Category 2 with maximum sustained winds near 110 mph as of Monday afternoon. The track has shifted slightly westward, with the center now forecast to pass just west of Niihau and Kauaʻi overnight Monday–Tuesday rather than making direct landfall on Kauaʻi. A Hurricane Warning for Kauaʻi County and Niihau remains in effect. Governor Josh Green has declared a State of Emergency for the state, activated 129 Hawaii National Guard members, and pre-positioned six high-water rescue vehicles on Kauaʻi. Heavy rain of 8–12 inches is expected across Kauaʻi County with isolated amounts up to 14 inches, sufficient to trigger flash flooding and mudslides. Life-threatening surf will affect south and west-facing shores. Damaging hurricane-force winds are still expected on or near the center track. Power outages are considered likely. The Hawaii Emergency Management Agency is maintaining emergency shelters across Kauaʻi. All flights into Lihue Airport (LIH) remain cancelled through Tuesday morning.

major_events.name: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods — ONGOING: 1,318+ Dead; 5,614+ Missing; Barrier Lake Risk; 5,000+ Rescuers
major_events.status: 1,318+ DEAD · 5,614+ MISSING · BARRIER LAKE RISK · RESCUE ONGOING · NO MATERIAL TOLL CHANGE
major_events.impact: The combined death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse holds at 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet. No material new toll figure was reported September 7–8. Flood debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn that surrounding glaciers may still collapse. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police continue search operations.

major_events.name: Malaysia / SE Asia Wildfire Haze — ESCALATION: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Activated (Highest Tier); ~300,000 ha Active Fires in Kalimantan; 1.4 Million Students Remote; Serian Emergency; Philippines and Brunei Impacted
major_events.status: ASEAN LEVEL 3 ALERT (HIGHEST) · ~300K HA ACTIVE FIRES · 1.4M STUDENTS REMOTE · SERIAN EMERGENCY ONGOING
major_events.impact: ASEAN has activated its Level 3 transboundary haze alert — its highest tier — covering Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the Philippines, as approximately 300,000 hectares of active fire continue to burn in Indonesian Kalimantan based on MODIS and VIIRS hot-spot analysis. The Level 3 designation signals a high risk of severe cross-border haze and triggers coordinated regional emergency response. An estimated 1.4 million students across Malaysia continue to attend school remotely. Malaysia's formal emergency in the Serian Division of Sarawak (Air Pollutant Index peaked at 521 on September 4) remains in effect. Cloud-seeding operations continue. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry has reported 717+ fire hot spots nationally since August 1. El Niño-driven dry conditions are forecast to sustain elevated fire risk across Kalimantan through early October.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire and Drought Emergency — ONGOING: 649,474 ha Burned; Very Extreme Fire Danger Continuing; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
major_events.status: ONGOING · 649,474 HA (UP FROM 647,579) · VERY EXTREME FIRE DANGER · RHINE LOWEST SINCE 1880
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 649,474 hectares as of the September 7 data refresh, up slightly from 647,579 ha reported September 4. Very extreme fire danger continues across Iberia, France, the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues to curtail output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. The record August 2026 heat (1.65°C above pre-industrial per Copernicus) is sustaining fire weather conditions well into September.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — ONGOING: 299+ Dead (Including 140 Children); Peak Season; 2–3 More September Pulse Events Forecast
major_events.status: ONGOING · 299+ DEAD · PEAK MONSOON · 2–3 MORE SEPTEMBER SPELLS FORECAST
major_events.impact: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299 (including 140 children) per the most recent NDMA reporting. This year's rainfall is running 50–60% heavier than the comparable period last year. NDMA continues to forecast 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the season's climatological peak.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — HELD: ~25,163 Hectares; Phased Re-Entry Ongoing; Summerland Partial Orders Active
major_events.status: HELD · ~25,163 HA · PHASED RE-ENTRY · SUMMERLAND PARTIAL ORDERS
major_events.impact: The Bald Range wildfire near Summerland maintains its HELD classification with no material change in fire extent (~25,163 ha). The Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen EOC is conducting phased re-entry planning. Wildfire crews are making progress toward containment, but it was not yet clear when all residents would be able to return. Peachland and Electoral Area West properties remain under an Evacuation Alert. Some portions of Summerland remain under Evacuation Orders.

weather.overview_html: Hurricane Lowell has weakened overnight to Category 2 (110 mph) as of Monday afternoon, but remains a serious threat: the center is now forecast to pass just west of Niihau and Kauaʻi overnight Monday–Tuesday; a Hurricane Warning for Kauaʻi County and Niihau remains in effect; and Governor Josh Green has declared a State of Emergency, activating 129 National Guard members and deploying six high-water vehicles to Kauaʻi. Life-threatening surf, damaging winds, and 8–12 inches of rain (isolated 14 inches) are forecast; power outages are considered likely; LIH remains closed through Tuesday morning. A new regional escalation in Southeast Asia: ASEAN has activated its Level 3 transboundary haze alert — its highest tier — covering Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Brunei, as approximately 300,000 hectares of active fire continues to burn in Indonesian Kalimantan. The remainder of the active board is unchanged: Nepal–Tibet GLOF at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing and Europe at 649,474 ha burned with very extreme fire danger continuing.

Critically, the track has shifted slightly westward, and the center is now forecast to pass just west of Niihau and Kauaʻi overnight Monday–Tuesday rather than making direct landfall — but a Hurricane Warning for Kauaʻi County and Niihau remains in effect and life-threatening impacts are still expected. items.headline: SE Asia Haze Escalation: ASEAN Activates Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert (Highest Tier) — ~300,000 ha Active Fire in Kalimantan; Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Philippines Affected; 1.4 Million Students Remote; Cloud-Seeding Continuing
items.summary: ASEAN has activated its Level 3 transboundary haze alert — its highest emergency tier — for the southern region, as fires burning across Kalimantan and Sumatra drive severe cross-border haze into Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the Philippines. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fire are detected in Indonesian Kalimantan based on MODIS and VIIRS hot-spot analysis, releasing over 23 million metric tons of carbon emissions since late August. The Level 3 alert triggers coordinated regional response including emergency diplomatic consultations, joint firefighting resource sharing, and coordinated cloud-seeding operations. An estimated 1.4 million Malaysian students continue remote learning. Malaysia's Serian Division emergency (Air Pollutant Index peaked at 521) remains in effect. El Niño-driven dry conditions are forecast to sustain elevated fire risk through early October.

renewables.overview_html: The biggest new development on September 8 is India’s Central Electricity Authority proposing mandatory co-located energy storage for all new solar and wind projects commissioned from 1 July 2027 — a landmark grid-stability mandate for the world’s third-largest electricity market. Under the draft, Phase 1 (July 2027–June 2029) requires at least 10% of installed capacity as at minimum 2-hour storage; Phase 2 (July 2029) raises the minimum duration to 4 hours. On the M&A front, Qualitas Energy has agreed to acquire Cero Generation’s entire European platform — 5.8 GW across the UK, Italy, and Spain (over 2 GW operational or ready-to-build plus 3.8 GW development) — from Macquarie Group. And Heerema Marine Contractors completed the full 100-monopile and two-substation-jacket foundation campaign for the Equinor–Polenergia Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind farms in the Polish Baltic Sea, with first power targeted for 2027.

items.source: PV-Tech / SolarQuarter / Mercom India / CEA India
items.headline: India CEA Draft Regulation: Mandatory Co-located Energy Storage for All New Solar & Wind From July 2027 — 10% of Capacity, 2-Hour Minimum; Phase 2 (July 2029) Raises to 4-Hour Duration; 15% Grid-Forming Inverters Required; World’s Largest Renewables Market Pivots on Grid Stability
items.summary: India's Central Electricity Authority issued a draft regulation on September 3, 2026 mandating that all ground-mounted solar and onshore wind power plants commissioned on or after July 1, 2027 must install co-located battery energy storage systems (BESS) equivalent to at least 10% of the plant's installed capacity with a minimum discharge duration of 2 hours. Phase 2 (from July 1, 2029) maintains the 10% storage ratio but raises the minimum duration to 4 hours. Additionally, at least 15% of inverters in new renewable energy plants must be equipped with grid-forming control technology from July 2027. India, which added over 100 GW of solar and wind capacity between 2023 and 2026, faces acute midday solar surplus and evening ramp challenges on its increasingly solar-heavy grid. The draft remains subject to public consultation before finalization.

items.headline: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s Core European Platform From Macquarie Group — 5.8 GW in UK, Italy, Spain; 2+ GW Operating / Construction / RTB; 3.8 GW Development Pipeline; Cero Generation Brand Retained as Independent Portfolio Company
items.summary: Qualitas Energy has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cero Generation's core European platform from Macquarie Group, acquiring a 5.8 GW portfolio of solar PV and battery storage assets across the UK, Italy, and Spain. The transaction includes over 2 GW of assets currently in operation, under construction, or at the ready-to-build stage, plus a further 3.8 GW development pipeline. Cero Generation, established by Macquarie in 2021 as a standalone European independent power producer, will continue to operate under the Cero Generation brand as a portfolio company of Qualitas Energy, with existing teams in London, Milan, and Madrid retained. The deal is expected to close within the coming months, subject to regulatory approvals. This represents the largest European renewables platform transfer by Macquarie since the firm established dedicated infrastructure vehicles in Europe.

items.source: OffshoreWind.biz / Windtech International / Energy Monitor / Heerema
items.headline: Heerema Completes Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 Offshore Foundation Campaign — 100 Monopiles + 2 Offshore Substation Jackets; Equinor–Polenergia JV; Polish Baltic Sea; First Power 2027; Commercial Operations 2028
items.summary: Heerema Marine Contractors has completed the offshore foundation installation campaign for the Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind farms in the Polish Baltic Sea, successfully installing 100 monopile foundations, 100 transition pieces, and 2 offshore substation jackets using the semi-submersible crane vessel Thialf over a four-month offshore campaign. At peak activity, approximately 15 vessels operated simultaneously across the project area. The Bałtyk 2 and 3 project is a joint venture between Equinor and Polenergia. Heerema will return this winter to install the Bałtyk 2 Offshore Substation, followed by the Bałtyk 3 Offshore Substation in summer 2027. First power generation from Bałtyk 2 and 3 is anticipated in 2027, with full commercial operations planned for 2028.

items.headline: CIP and Gawara Baya Energy: AUD 1.7 Billion Queensland Wind + BESS — 408 MW Wind Farm and 104 MW / 416 MWh Battery; Australia’s Largest Announced Wind+Storage Development; Financial Close Q3 2026; Commercial Operations 2028
items.summary: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Gawara Baya Energy announced the financial close of an AUD 1.7 billion (approximately USD 1.1 billion) wind-plus-battery storage project in Queensland, Australia on September 1 — the largest announced wind and storage co-located development in Australia. The project comprises a 408 MW onshore wind farm co-located with a 104 MW / 416 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). Power purchase agreements cover a portion of output; the remainder sells into the Queensland National Electricity Market. Queensland's energy transition target requires 80% renewables by 2035. Construction is targeted to commence in late 2026 with commercial operations by 2028.

items.headline: ENGIE Chile Financial Close: 251 MW / 1,004 MWh Standalone BESS for USD 384 Million — Chile’s Largest Single Battery Storage Contract; Grid Stabilization on Atacama Solar-Heavy Grid; Operations 2027
items.summary: ENGIE Chile reached financial close on September 1 on a 251 MW / 1,004 MWh standalone battery energy storage system project for USD 384 million — Chile's largest single BESS contract. The system is designed to provide grid stabilization, frequency regulation, and energy shifting on Chile's Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (SEN), which is heavily weighted toward variable solar generation from the Atacama Desert. The project addresses the SEN's growing challenge of managing midday solar surpluses and evening ramping demand — a problem that has caused negative prices in peak solar hours. Commercial operations are expected in 2027.

items.headline: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) First Monopile Installed — 795 MW RWE/TotalEnergies JV; 53 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbines; 53 km Off Dutch Coast; 1 Million Dutch Households by 2028; Transition-Piece-Less Design
items.summary: The offshore installation vessel Les Alizés successfully installed the first of 53 monopiles for OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) on September 1, 53 km west of IJmuiden in the Dutch North Sea. The 795 MW project is a joint venture between RWE and TotalEnergies, using 53 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines. The project uses innovative transition-piece-less monopiles, where turbine towers bolt directly to the monopile without a transition piece, reducing steel per foundation. Installation of all 53 monopiles is expected to complete by early 2027; turbine installation in 2027; fully operational by early 2028, supplying approximately 1 million Dutch households.

science.overview_html: Two new papers enter the digest this cycle. arXiv:2609.02566 (Nath, Schemm, Haynes, Shuckburgh, Webb — Met Office / Cambridge) couples the Met Office Unified Model with distributed reinforcement learning agents, reducing 500-hPa geopotential height MAE by up to 45.8% at +6 h lead time in a nudged-training framework — the first demonstration of closed-loop RL correction operating inside an operational global NWP system. arXiv:2609.04427 (Pacey, Miralles, Hamann, Martius — Univ. Bern / MeteoSwiss) shows that increasing hail nowcasting training-data volume raises skill by up to 25 minutes at later lead times — a larger gain than any architecture change — and that data augmentation interacts non-monotonically with dataset size. These join the week’s standing papers: WeatherNext 3 at 5-km hourly from raw observations; TC-Next cutting cyclone intensity error 3–6×; IMERG fine-tuning for a 57% Brier skill score gain on extreme rainfall; and CloudCast v2 extending AI cloud cover forecasting to 12-hour lead time.

items.source: arXiv / Met Office / University of Cambridge / University of Edinburgh
items.headline: arXiv 2609.02566: Online Reinforcement Learning in the Met Office Unified Model via Distributed RL Agent Coupling — First Closed-Loop RL Correction in an Operational Global NWP System; 45.8% Z500 MAE Reduction at +6 h; DDPG Actor Across 70 Vertical Levels; Numerically Stable
items.meta: Nath, Schemm, Haynes, Shuckburgh, Webb (Met Office / Cambridge / Edinburgh) · arXiv:2609.02566 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: This paper couples the Met Office Unified Model (UM) with distributed reinforcement learning agents through rank-local tensors. A DDPG actor shares weights across the 70 vertical model levels of each atmospheric column and applies bounded potential-temperature corrections to model tendencies. Training uses nudging toward the UKMO operational analysis as an immediate counterfactual target across ten nudged training forecasts; the frozen policy is then evaluated in non-nudged free-running forecasts. Relative to a matched native UM forecast at +6 h, the learnt policy reduces 500-hPa geopotential height MAE in four of six latitude bands, including reductions of 45.8% and 40.8% in the most responsive bands. The coupled workflow completes training and remains numerically stable throughout. This is the first demonstration of online closed-loop RL operating inside an operational global NWP model — bridging the gap between offline ML parameterisation and live model correction.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.04427: Input Data Sensitivity in Deep-Learning Hail Nowcasting — More Training Years Beats Architecture Changes; +25 Minutes Skill at Late Lead Times; Augmentation Degrades Smaller Datasets; Spatiotemporal CNN Framework Over Switzerland
items.meta: Pacey, Miralles, Hamann, Martius (Univ. Bern / MeteoSwiss) · arXiv:2609.04427 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how input data choices affect deep-learning hail nowcasting skill in a spatiotemporal neural network framework, without changing model architecture. Sensitivity experiments assess the impact of training-data volume (years), random data augmentation (mirroring and rotation), and the number of input timesteps. Key results: increasing training data years substantially improves forecast skill by up to 25 minutes at later lead times — a larger gain than any architectural modification; data augmentation improves performance for larger datasets but interestingly degrades performance for smaller ones, suggesting augmentation interacts non-monotonically with dataset size; sensitivity to the number of input timesteps is weaker than sensitivity to training volume. The findings have direct practical implications for operational hail warning systems, indicating that investments in longer training archives yield higher returns than model complexity increases for this high-impact severe weather application.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 5-km Global AI Weather Model Trains on Raw Observations; 60% Better Precipitation vs. WN2; 100-m Wind-Height Forecasts; Tops Brightband WeatherBench; Live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based AI models and shrinking it to 3–4 hours with hourly forecast cycles. Resolution: 5 km for key surface variables, 10 km for other surface variables, 25 km for atmospheric variables, and explicit 100-meter hub-height wind forecasts for wind turbine applications alongside cloud cover and solar radiation for grid operators. WeatherNext 3 has 2.4× more parameters than WeatherNext 2. Precipitation evaluation shows CRPS improvements of up to 60% against IMERG and 50% Brier score reduction versus NWP baselines at early lead times. On Brightband's Operational WeatherBench, WeatherNext 3 ranks first across temperature, wind speed, and humidity. Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Google Earth Engine.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.02085 (TC-Next): Zero-Shot Multimodal Cyclone Forecasting — Trained Only on GraphCast/Western Pacific; Cuts Track Error 15–44% and Intensity Error 3–6× vs. Conventional Trackers; Transfers Without Retraining to Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES
items.meta: Wang, Chen, Luo, Kim, Chang · arXiv:2609.02085 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: TC-Next is a multimodal deep learning model that forecasts tropical cyclone track and intensity at 6–24 h lead times by jointly leveraging a foundation model's atmospheric forecast fields (kinematic and thermodynamic) and GridSat infrared satellite imagery. Trained exclusively on GraphCast forecast fields over the Western Pacific, TC-Next lowers track error by 15–44% and intensity error by a factor of 3–6 relative to the conventional rule-based tracker TempestExtremes. Critically, when applied zero-shot — without retraining — to forecast fields from Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES, TC-Next remains substantially ahead of TempestExtremes on both track and intensity, demonstrating strong model-agnostic generalization.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210: Fine-Tuning AI Weather Model With IMERG Precipitation Observations Improves Medium-Range CRPS by Up to 19% and Extreme Rainfall Brier Skill by 57%; Tropical Storms and Drizzle Also Improved
items.meta: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain · arXiv:2609.03210 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: This paper fine-tunes a graph-transformer AI weather prediction architecture directly with IMERG precipitation observational data at 0.25° resolution. Results: medium-range CRPS improves by up to 19%; Brier skill score for extreme rainfall prediction improves by 57% globally over state-of-the-art operational NWP models. The fine-tuned model also demonstrates superior skill for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events. The approach is directly relevant to the acute precipitation hazards active in this digest: Hurricane Lowell threatening Hawaii, Pakistan's monsoon, and Nepal's ongoing flood response.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecast — GloSea6 Underestimates TC Frequency, Tracks, Lifetime, and Intensity; Largest Errors in August; Downscaling Partially Corrects Bias
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates the characteristics of tropical cyclones in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6, the operational seasonal-to-sub-seasonal forecasting model of the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), over the western North Pacific during JJAS 1993–2016. GloSea6 is found to underestimate TC frequency, tracks, lifetime, and intensity across all months, with the most significant errors occurring in August. The paper evaluates whether dynamical downscaling to higher resolution can recover the lost skill for track and intensity. The results are directly relevant to the current Super El Niño season, during which TC forecast accuracy is critical for Hawaii, the Philippines, and Japan.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Winner MicroEnsemble (Microsoft-Led) Post-Processes ECMWF Dynamics With AI; Annual Awards Ceremony September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition phase: August 2025–September 2026 · Annual awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international competition for AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting operating from August 2025 to September 2026 — is concluding its first year, with an annual highlights and awards ceremony scheduled for September 24. Forty-two teams from 30+ countries submitted real-time global sub-seasonal forecasts at 1.5° resolution, providing quintile probabilities for weekly-mean temperature, precipitation, and sea level pressure for the Days 19–25 and Days 26–32 windows. The DJF 2025/26 period winner was MicroEnsemble, a Microsoft-led team whose approach uses AI to post-process state-of-the-art dynamical ECMWF forecasts — a hybrid AI-physical approach. ECMWF's own AIFS-SUBS submission extended skilful MJO forecasts by 8 days using approximately 200× less energy at inference than the dynamical model.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud Cover Forecasting Extended From 1–3 h to 12 h Lead Time; 10% MAE Reduction Over CloudCast v1; 43% Bias Reduction; 15-Minute Temporal and 4-km Spatial Resolution Over Scandinavia
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends the original CloudCast machine learning nowcasting system — which forecasted cloud cover at 1–3 hour lead times — to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution. The model is trained and evaluated over Scandinavia using MSG satellite data. Key results: 10% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) versus CloudCast v1; 43% reduction in systematic bias in the Scandinavian domain; improved skill at extended 6–12 h lead times where the original system degraded most sharply. Longer cloud cover forecasts have direct applications for solar power ramp forecasting, aviation, and solar resource assessment — important as Northern European grids integrate increasing shares of variable PV generation.

items.source: arXiv / Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD 2026
items.headline: arXiv 2609.00847: First Comprehensive Checklist for Energy and Carbon Footprints of ML/AI in Earth System Modeling; Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Presented at GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026 Naples
items.meta: Dainelli, Mozaffari, Castaño et al. (BSC Earth Dept.) · arXiv:2609.00847 · September 1, 2026 · GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026, Naples
items.summary: As machine learning finds its way into nearly every aspect of Earth system modeling, this Barcelona Supercomputing Center paper provides the first comprehensive checklist for ML/AI practitioners to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their applications. The checklist is organized around successive pipeline stages — data curation, model architecture, training regime, inference, and deployment — with curated metrics for estimating energy consumption and carbon footprint at each stage. The work is timely given the explosive growth of compute-intensive neural weather models such as WeatherNext 3, GraphCast, and AIFS. Presented at the GREEN-AI workshop of ECML PKDD 2026 in Naples.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end AI weather system probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder capturing aleatoric uncertainty; (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor capturing epistemic uncertainty. A law-of-total-variance decomposition attributes forecast spread to each source. Key result: probabilistic fine-tuning improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension.

items.title: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s 5.8 GW European Solar + BESS Platform From Macquarie Group — UK, Italy, Spain; Largest European Renewables Platform Transfer of 2026; Cero Brand Retained
items.body_html: Qualitas Energy signed a definitive agreement on September 7 to acquire Cero Generation’s entire European platform from Macquarie Group, taking on a 5.8 GW portfolio of solar PV and battery storage assets across the UK, Italy, and Spain. The deal includes over 2 GW in operation, under construction, or at the ready-to-build stage, plus 3.8 GW in active development. Cero Generation was established by Macquarie in 2021 as a standalone European IPP and will continue to operate under the Cero brand as a Qualitas portfolio company, retaining offices and teams in London, Milan, and Madrid. The transaction is the largest European renewables platform exit by an infrastructure fund in 2026 and reflects the ongoing consolidation of mid-scale European solar and BESS developers into larger specialist owners. Closing is expected within several months, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — Dedicated ILS, Structured Reinsurance, and Capital Markets Unit; Responds to Record $171B Verisk AAL Benchmark and Growing Alternative Capacity Demand
items.body_html: Howden Re launched its International Alternative Solutions (IAS) practice on September 6, a dedicated unit consolidating ILS placement, catastrophe bond issuance, collateralised reinsurance, and structured capital capabilities under a single leadership team. The launch comes as Verisk’s new $171 billion average annual insured loss benchmark reinforces broker and cedant demand for alternative capacity beyond traditional reinsurance limits. Hurricane Lowell’s overnight approach to Kauaʻi provides real-time illustration of the Super El Niño-driven exposure escalation that is reshaping cat reinsurance pricing and structure.

items.title: Swiss Re: Data Centers and AI Workloads Create $200 Billion Premium Opportunity for Property Insurers; Renewables Integration Compounds Risk Complexity; Presented at Monte Carlo Rendez-vous
items.body_html: Swiss Re released a research report at the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous on September 5 calculating that data centers and AI workloads represent a USD 200 billion global premium opportunity for property and casualty insurers over the next decade, driven by capital expenditure growth in hyperscaler infrastructure, increasingly dense equipment values, and emerging AI-driven operational exposures. The report identifies three layers of compounding risk: physical climate risk to data center locations (flood, wildfire, extreme heat affecting cooling systems); grid reliability risk as renewables integration creates frequency and voltage events; and cyber-physical risk from AI model failure cascades. Swiss Re argues that the insurance industry needs parametric and structured capacity mechanisms to underwrite these risks at scale, and that traditional property per-occurrence limits are structurally insufficient for large hyperscaler campuses.

items.title: Cyclic Materials Closes $75 Million Series C Led by T. Rowe Price to Scale US Rare Earth Recycling — Total Equity Now $237 Million; Arizona Facility Operational Q3 2026; South Carolina Campus Breaking Ground Q4; Critical Supply for Wind Turbines and EV Magnets
items.body_html: Cyclic Materials, a Canadian rare earth recycling company, closed a $75 million Series C financing round announced September 2, 2026, led by accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, bringing total equity funding to $237 million. Strategic investor ERI joined the round alongside existing backers Microsoft, Amazon, and others. Cyclic’s Hub-and-Spoke system recovers rare earth materials from permanent magnets in end-of-life wind turbines, EV motors, and manufacturing scrap. An Arizona magnet separation and critical mineral recycling plant is expected to begin operations during Q3 2026, with a South Carolina integrated rare earth recycling campus breaking ground in Q4 2026.
items.source_html: Cyclic Materials / Metal Tech News

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%); 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from the prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%.
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: Artemis London 2026: Cat Bond and ILS Market Well-Positioned for Disciplined Growth; AFME Calls for ILS to Back Climate Policies; 220 Attendees, 120+ Organizations
items.body_html: The Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1 convened approximately 220 attendees from more than 120 organizations across the ILS ecosystem. Speakers highlighted discipline in the catastrophe bond market and expected continued growth. The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME) called for ILS and catastrophe bonds as effective mechanisms for insurers to access new capital to back climate-related policies — directly relevant as the Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, released the same day, put average annual insured losses at a record $171 billion.
